programmes.d: Philippe Cousteau looks at ways scientists are measuring the health of our forests.
Philippe Cousteau looks at new ways of cultivating fresh, nutritious food.
We head to a winter wonderland in Banff, Alberta, Canada.
We look at different examples of cultural science.

Volcanic folklore is reflected in Mexican history. One of their ancient legends tells the story of the Aztec warrior Popocatépetl - a giant active volcano - who erupts to wake his sleeping princess Iztaccíhuatl, a neighboring extinct ice capped volcano.

In Indonesia we find regions where the air is so toxic that it's 40 times above human safe levels and sulphuric acid vents from the ground in dense yellowish clouds. Elsewhere, small volcanoes are so active, they are said to erupt every 15 minutes!
Japan is going through a seismic crisis after the devastating Tsunami of 2011. We look closely at two very dangerous volcanoes; both are considered to be in the top 5 most dangerous on the planet.
For people who live on active volcanoes, life has an element of impermanence to it. There is always the fear that one day their turn will come, and their home will be in the path of the volcano.
Humans refine and evolve weapons designs over the millennia to gain the upper hand.
Pioneering breakthroughs from across the globe shape the ability to travel.
The first data-recording device from over 5,000 years ago; how weaving creates binary code.
From living in caves to grand mansions, shelter has always been high on the list of priorities.
Almost every culture on Earth tells the story of an ancient flood – details vary but the basic plot is the same - An angry God wipes out an unrepentant population.

Superflares are amongst the greatest events of the Universe. These magnetic explosions can release energy millions of times greater than atomic bombs. They produce streams of highly energetic particles which can be highly destructive to life.
Hurricanes are one of the most destructive weather events to strike our planet and have the same power as a nuclear weapon.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: Exo Planets
programmes.d: As scientists and astronomers peer more closely and with evermore fidelity at nearby stars, they are discovering countless exo planets. How many Earth-like planets are out there? Could one of them hold life not so different from our own?

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: Edge of the Universe
programmes.d: The night sky is a time machine. The further we look out into the universe, the further back in time we reach. Most of what we see is actually dark matter and dark energy, but its nature eludes us ... for the moment.

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: The Astronauts
programmes.d: Who are these people that venture into space? Once they were test pilots, then scientists and engineers now teachers, politicians and paying tourists what does it take to earn the astronaut wings?

programmes.t: Space: The New Frontier: Space: Getting There
programmes.d: The new surge in space transportation, privately owned companies vying for government contracts and private entrepreneurs looking to build hotels in space.

Chances are, you are watching this program by satellite, one way or the other. Every day we use these wonders of human design, from communication and weather observation, to GPS and recourse management.
